currentContext.strengths: Backward-integrated model spanning design, engineering, manufacturing (concrete products, glazing/metal, interiors) and construction execution within a single framework, giving tight control over quality, coordination and delivery|Customers in both growing and mature markets place a premium on SOBHA's quality and reliability, which the in-house manufacturing capability is positioned to meet|Net cash position maintained during FY26 despite external volatility, indicating balance-sheet resilience
currentContext.strategies: Building institutional depth across talent, design, delivery and manufacturing to support scale while keeping delivery quality and standards consistent|Advancing learning and leadership development programmes (including at the Sobha Academy) to prepare for larger, more complex operations|Deploying digital project controls to refine scheduling and resource readiness across the project cycle|Using virtual design environments, including BIM-led review, to bring model precision and clash detection closer to the planning stage|Embedding AI-enabled monitoring for site safety/progress visibility and robotics-led applications for uniformity in repetitive construction processes|Continued investment in new machinery and specialised production capability within the backward-integration model to support quality benchmarks and timelines|Geographic expansion into new cities, having entered Greater Noida (SOBHA Aurum) and Mumbai (SOBHA Inizio) during FY26|Maintaining financial prudence and a net cash position amid external volatility and geopolitical uncertainty|Continuing focused CSR activities emphasising healthcare, education and housing for underserved communities|Following a consistent dividend pay-out policy while balancing deployment of internal accruals for growth against dividend payment|The Company maintains a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (listed among its governance policies, full text not reproduced in this bundle). For FY26, a dividend of Rs 6 per equity share (face value Rs 10) was placed before shareholders for approval at the AGM via an Ordinary Resolution declaring it 'be paid out of the profits of the Company'. The Company does not have a designated 'material subsidiary' under SEBI LODR and monitors subsidiaries via Audit Committee review of their financial statements, board-minutes circulation, and disclosure of significant transactions.
currentContext.expansion: SOBHA operates a fully backward-integrated manufacturing model - the company describes itself as the only real estate player in India with its own manufacturing facilities for building materials - spanning Glazing & Metal Works, Interiors, Concrete Products, and a Retail/Mattress division, each also servicing third-party clients as a profit centre. The Glazing and Metal Works facility in Bangalore (7.91 acres, ~99,943 sq ft) is supplemented by divisions in Kancheepuram (Tamil Nadu) and Sonepat (Haryana). The Interiors division runs two mechanised factories at Bommasandra, Bangalore, plus a division in Alwar, equipped with imported machinery from Spain, Italy and Germany. The Concrete Products division's Bangalore facility (8 acres, imported German/UK technology) has been supplemented by divisions in Gurgaon and Pune, and a newly added unit in Hosur. Retail sales include mattresses under the 'Sobha Restoplus' brand and home-furnishing packages under the 'metercube' sub-brand. Separately, in the Chairman's letter, management describes continued investment in new machinery and specialised production capability within the backward-integration model to support quality benchmarks and timelines, alongside real estate geographic expansion into Greater Noida (SOBHA Aurum) and Mumbai (SOBHA Inizio) during FY26.

risks.note: SOBHA operates in twelve cities in real estate, but a sizeable portion of real-estate sales is generated in Bangalore; a decline in that market or a shift in customer loyalty there could adversely affect business and operating results

The contractual business depends solely on orders from corporate entities, with a substantial portion of contractual revenue generated from major clients in the information technology sector, exposing it to IT-sector demand cycles

Land is a primary input for construction; non-availability of appropriate parcels at strategic locations and reasonable prices can raise costs, while a drop in land prices could erode the book value of land held, affecting profitability

Real estate development is controlled by local, state and central regulatory bodies (zoning, permitted land use, fire safety, building height, utility access); delays in obtaining approvals under these laws expose the business to higher risk
SOBHA is involved in legal proceedings relating to lands it owns and claims on taxation matters; an adverse decision could significantly impact business, prospects and financials

The residential real estate sector is highly competitive and fragmented; adequate information on smaller/medium competitors' projects may not be available, creating a risk of underestimating market supply

risks.risk: Macroeconomic sensitivity (interest rate, inflation, exchange rate)
risks.note: Changes in interest rates can raise the Company's cost of borrowing and impact profitability, while a sluggish economy or sector-specific downturn (e.g. in IT/ITES) can reduce demand and sales for residential and contractual projects

Real estate properties can take variable time to liquidate depending on quality and location, so the Company may not be able to liquidate assets promptly in response to adverse economic or market conditions

one-line thesis: Landmark quarter: highest-ever presales of INR3,656cr (+76% YoY) on well-prepared launches of SOBHA One World (Bangalore) and Crescent (Gurgaon), with revenue +48% and PAT +3.8x (INR50.7cr). Reported margin is still depressed (~9.7% EBITDA) but management reiterates a sharp H2 ramp to 17-20% by exit-Q4 as high-margin FY23-vintage projects complete, backed by a net-cash balance sheet (net-debt ratio −0.14) and INR20,553cr of unrecognized sold-revenue. Key watch: margin delivery, collections catch-up, and labour-cost/availability (Karnataka +60% min-wage; April-May labour shortage already dented milestone billing).

| Total income | INR1,330cr | +~48% | Real estate revenue INR1,107cr (+60% vs INR690cr); contractual/mfg/retail INR171cr (vs INR162cr) |
| EBITDA / margin | ~9.7% margin | — | Still low; guided to 17-20% by exit-Q4 as high-margin projects complete |
| PAT | INR50.7cr | +~276% (vs INR13.5cr) | Boosted by higher RE revenue recognition + mix + cost discipline |
| Order/earnings visibility | INR20,553cr unrecognized sold-revenue | — | Projected receivable+unsold ~INR31,000cr; est. remaining cost INR19,000cr → projected margin cash flow ~INR12,000cr |
| Cash / net debt | Net cash INR659cr; net-debt ratio −0.14 | — | Gross debt INR1,110cr; cash INR1,769cr; avg borrowing cost 7.62% |
> Operational cash inflow INR1,924cr (+8.2%); RE collections INR1,756cr (vs INR1,599cr); net operating CF INR312cr. Quarter had net cash OUTFLOW of INR149cr from planned land (INR370cr) + capex (INR70cr). Collections modest vs presales — new-sale collections skewed to quarter-end + milestone-billing shortfall from April/May labour shortage.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Presales growth:** at least +30% for FY27 (possibly slightly better if launches land on time).
- **Margin:** significantly better sequentially in H2; Q2 similar to Q1 (~depends on completions); by exit-Q4 targeting ~17-20% EBITDA (from ~9.7% now).
- **Launches:** 9 projects / ~8.2 msf in remaining FY27 (~INR12,000cr GDV) — 4 Bangalore (~3 msf), 2 NCR (~2 msf), 1 Hyderabad (~1.7 msf), 2 Kerala (~1.5 msf). Crescent Phase-2 late-Q3/Q4; Greater Noida to launch this FY.
- **Completions:** 6-6.5 msf in FY27 vs 5.4 msf FY26 (~20% higher).
- **Net debt:** to remain ~0 (net-cash) for the year.
- **Land capex:** ~INR1,500-1,600cr for FY27 (vs INR1,160cr FY26); INR370cr already spent in Q1.
- **Operating cash flow:** aiming toward ~INR2,000cr (marginal, averaged over next few years).
- **Other businesses (contractual/mfg/rental):** FY27 revenue ~similar to FY26.
- **Funding:** INR1,000cr NCDs approved — to be drawn in ≥2 tranches over next couple of quarters as acquisitions firm up.
order book & pipeline:
- Forthcoming launch pipeline: 20.77 msf across 17 projects; near-term confident set = 9 projects / 8.2 msf in FY27.
- Unsold inventory: 14.94 msf.
- Q1 launches (3 projects, Bangalore+Gurgaon): 6.89 msf combined, ~INR10,000cr potential sale value.
- Unrecognized sold-revenue backlog INR20,553cr underpins multi-year revenue visibility.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Residential (core):** SOBHA One World (3,484 homes / 47.4 acres; released 3.4 msf, sold ~40% at launch; 45% of quarter's sales); SOBHA Crescent Gurgaon (~60% sold in Q1); Sacred Grove (plotted, Bangalore); Rivana (Noida) steady post-launch.
- **Contractual, manufacturing & retail (backward integration):** ~INR170-171cr revenue; good order-book visibility; differentiator vs peers; FY27 run-rate ~flat vs FY26.
- **Commercial rental:** ~INR23cr total income; evaluating retaining a ~0.6 msf Gurgaon commercial project for rental (removed from sale pipeline pending decision).
- **New BD this quarter:** Mumbai (1.3 acres, INR180cr outright) + Greater Noida (JV, authority+landowner dues paid); combined GDV ~INR2,700-3,000cr.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Geographic expansion into high-growth micro-markets (NCR scaling to highest-ever; Hyderabad, Kerala, new Mumbai foothold).
- Optionality to convert the Gurgaon commercial asset (full TDR in hand) into a rental annuity rather than sale.
- Land-bank build-out (INR1,500-1,600cr FY27) — greater joint-development mix lowers capital intensity but also lowers marginal cash-flow margin.
margins & cost dynamics: Reported EBITDA ~9.7% is the trough; margin expansion thesis rests on completing high-margin FY23-vintage projects (revenue recognized on completion). Forthcoming-project marginal cash flow guidance cut to INR68.3bn (from ~INR86bn) due to (a) higher joint-development mix and (b) high-margin own-land Hoskote rolling off the forthcoming set. Cost pressure: Karnataka minimum-wage +60% (May) under evaluation — technician force largely above minimum wage, expected to be absorbed within project budgets. April-May labour shortage delayed some completion milestones.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- FY27 completions target 6-6.5 msf (vs 5.4 msf FY26). Q1 completed 677 homes / 1.08 msf.
- Land spend FY27 ~INR1,500-1,600cr; new-land value typically ~15% of project sale value.
- Slippage watch: Mumbai project launch timing uncertain (approvals — excluded from the 8.2 msf FY27 plan); labour-driven milestone delays.
capital allocation: Net-cash balance sheet (net-debt ratio −0.14) with low 7.62% borrowing cost. Prioritizes: strong/liquid balance sheet, improved collections, disciplined land acquisition. INR1,000cr NCDs approved for tranche-wise acquisition funding. No dividend/buyback commentary. Balances land aggression against maintaining ~0 net debt for the year.
risks & watch-items:
- **Margin execution:** H2 17-20% target is a repeat of last quarter's H2-revival guidance — must actually land via completions.
- **Collections lag:** presales strong but Q1 collections modest (quarter-end skew + labour-driven milestone-billing shortfall).
- **Labour:** Karnataka +60% min-wage cost impact "yet to be assessed"; April-May shortage affected billing.
- **Mix dilution:** rising joint-development share lowers marginal cash-flow margins vs own-land projects.
- **Launch/approval slippage:** Mumbai timing uncertain; overall growth depends on launches landing on schedule.
- **Supply/cycle:** demand "stable/reasonably good"; management watching how competing supply develops.
management quality / tone: Confident and execution-focused; attributes the strong quarter to launch preparation, not just market timing. Transparent about the collections shortfall, the labour issue, the margin trough, and the marginal-cash-flow reduction (JD mix + Hoskote roll-off). Reiterates prudence — net-cash discipline, tranche-wise NCDs, absorbing wage inflation within budgets.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Headline presales (+76%) far outrun revenue (+48%) and collections — the value is stored in the INR20,553cr unrecognized backlog; the earnings/margin inflection is a completion-driven H2/FY27 event, not a Q1 one.
- The forthcoming-project margin cut (INR86bn→INR68.3bn) is structural (more JD, less own-land like Hoskote) — a quieter negative under the record-presales headline.
- Net cash of only INR659cr despite record sales reflects deliberate front-loaded land investment (net outflow INR149cr in the quarter) — growth capex, not weakness.
- Gurgaon commercial asset possibly shifting from sale to rental annuity — a small model-mix signal worth tracking.

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.
